title: Exploiting novel options for triple negative breast cancer treatment: combination studies of classical therapeutics with the chromene derivative SMT01
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most prevalent cancer worldwide, with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) emerging as the most aggressive subtype. High relapse and recurrence rates, occurrence of distant metastasis, limited therapeutic options and the lowest 5-year overall survival rates among all BC subtypes, characterize TNBC. Novel and effective treatments capable of overcoming toxicity associated with classical treatments, as well as resistance events, are urgently needed. In this line, there is a growing interest in using combinations of classical treatments with novel anticancer agents, to increase treatment effectiveness while reducing their side effects. Chromenes, extensively studied as potential therapeutic compounds in several diseases, demonstrated cytotoxic and antiproliferative properties in cancer cells. These anticancer effects have been validated in multiple preclinical and clinical studies in the last years, including in TNBC. An initial screening of a chromene-based family synthesized by our team’s chemists identified SMT01 as a new lead compound with anticancer potential for TNBC. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of the combination of a classical chemotherapeutic agent used to treat TNBC patients – doxorubicin (DOX) – with SMT01. For this, the half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) of each drug alone was determined, performing cell viability assays in two TNBC cell lines (Hs578T and MDA-MB-231) and their combined effect using a matrix model and the CompuSyn software was also assessed. A synergistic combination, capable of significantly reducing DOX EC50, was obtained. Additionally, in vitro experiments to characterize the drug combination effects on several cancer hallmarks were performed. The most effective drug combinations promoted a significant reduction in cell proliferation and invasion, arrest in cell cycle and induction of cell death by apoptosis in the two TNBC cell lines. In conclusion, this work presents a preliminary evaluation of a novel therapeutic approach that seems to inhibit multiple aggressiveness features on TNBC cell lines. The identified synergistic drug combinations hold promise for enhancing therapeutic effectiveness of the classical treatment, minimizing toxicity and ultimately contributing to improved treatment outcomes for TNBC patients

title: Tau protein in CRH neurons as a modulator of memory consolidation
abstract: Tau, a microtubule-associated protein within CRH neurons has a profound impact on various aspects of brain function, including memory consolidation, neural dynamics, cognitive and emotional functions, and neuronal structural integrity. An innovative CRH-Tau-cKO model, characterized by its precise targeting with spatial control, functional analysis capabilities, and translational relevance was used. This novel model, combined with multidisciplinary approaches, unravels new pathways for comprehending the complex processes underpinning neuron’s role in neural mechanisms, brain circuits and behavioral regulation. Empirical evidence emerges, illustrating the substantial influence of Tau deletion within CRH neurons on spontaneous neural activity. Cognitive impairments and emotional phenotypes in CRH-Tau-cKO mice further emphasize the pivotal role of Tau in regulating cognitive and emotional functions, through its role in neuronal structure and synaptic function. Moreover, structural abnormalities are unveiled in key brain regions, including the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), hippocampus, and amygdala, due to Tau deletion within CRH neurons. These structural aberrations hold significant implications for stress responses, cognitive function, and emotional regulation, reinforcing the multifaceted role of Tau in preserving neuronal structural integrity and its relevance in various neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions. Our multiscale analysis included qRT-PCR, western blots, neuromorphological studies and behavioural studies. The results gathered provided invaluable insights into the complex interplay of Tau within CRH neurons, shedding light on memory consolidation, neural dynamics, cognitive and emotional functions, and neuronal structural integrity.

title: The role of astrocytic metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 in depressive-like behavior
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder is a highly prevalent psychiatric illness, that is characterized by the prevalence of negative emotional states induced by multiple factors, as chronic stress. The most used treatments for depression nowadays show limited efficacy and several side effects. Therefore, the discovery of new targets and new drugs is urgent. The glutamatergic system is responsible for rapid and excitatory transmission commonly associated with MDD. Astrocytes are glial cells that play an important role in modulating neurotransmission. These cells express receptors for neurotransmitters and, therefore, detect synaptic activity, process the signaling through somatic calcium levels increase, and release neuroactive molecules that modulate synaptic and neuronal activity. The metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) is the primary metabotropic excitatory receptor for glutamate in astrocytes. Despite its widely studied antidepressant properties in neurons, the role of this receptor in modulating glutamatergic systems in adults remains to be understood. Thus, in this dissertation, we focused on studying mGluR5 in hippocampal astrocytes by assessing loss- and gain- of astrocytic mGluR5 function in the context of a mouse model of depression. First, deletion of the mGluR5 gene was induced by viral-driven genetic recombination (AAV5:GFAP(0.7)iCre-T2A-mCherry) specifically into the dorsal hippocampus of a mouse model displaying the mGluR5 gene with flanked by loxP sites (dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5KO). Similarly, a model of mGluR5 overexpression in astrocytes was generated (dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5+) in C57BL/6J mice by viral approach to drive the overexpression of mGluR5 (AAV5:GFAP(0.7)-mGluR5minigene-FLAG). Then, the dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5KO model was subjected to a chronic stress protocol (uCMS). Behavioral characterization revealed the efficiency of the chronic stress protocol, which induced a depressive and anxious state in mice. Interestingly, the dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5KO mice group displayed partial resilience to the installation of the depressive phenotype. On the other hand, the dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5+ mouse model displayed protection against learned helplessness while also presenting an impairment in recognition memory and enhanced behavioral flexibility. The structural and molecular analysis of both models confirmed the efficient modulation of the levels of mGluR5 and the promotion of morphological alterations in astrocytes of the dorsal hippocampus of the dHIP:GFAP-mGluR5KO mice group. These findings point to the astrocytic mGluR5 in adulthood as an interesting target for the development of new studies and possible treatments for depression.

title: Impact of modulating hippocampal dentate gyrus adult-born cells in the context of depression and Psilocybin treatment
abstract: Adult brain cytogenesis, more specifically, the generation of new neurons (neurogenesis) and glial cells (gliogenesis) in the hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG) of rodents was shown to be compromised in animal models of neuropsychiatric disorders, such as Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), impacting on cognitive and emotional domains. Regarding MDD, the underlying causes of this condition are still not fully understood, and current treatments are not universally effective. Therefore, there is an urgent need to better understand the molecular mechanisms behind this disorder and develop more effective interventions. In this work, we developed a set of experiments to investigate the impact of optogenetic modulation of adult hippocampal DG newborn cells on a validated rat model of depression – the unpredictable chronic mild stress (uCMS) model. In this project, we evaluated whether, in rats, the modulation of new cells in the adult hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG) is relevant to the efficacy of a compound with therapeutic potential, Psilocybin, a tryptamine alkaloid found in various species of Psilocybe mushrooms, which has shown therapeutic potential in cases of treatment-resistant depression when compared to currently prescribed antidepressants. The present work has provided evidence that manipulating neurogenesis can influence emotional (anhedonic and anxious) and cognitive outcomes related to depression-like symptoms. Additionally, treatment with Psilocybin is able to reverse the hedonic and cognitive deficits induced by depression in rats, depending directly on hippocampal newborn cells. With this project we contributed to unraveling the contribution of DG adult-born cells for behavioral domains impaired in depressive-like animals, possibly helping to find alternative routes for developing better therapies for MDD.

title: Implementing a novel click-chemistry approach to assess brain regional and cell-specific brain phospholipase D activity
abstract: Lipids constitute a major portion of the brain and play a critical role in its function and structure, with key lipid alterations observed in neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), where studies implicate the phospholipase D (PLD) pathway. PLD isoenzyme PLD1 has been proposed as the major source of phosphatidic acid (PA) in the hippocampus, a brain structure vulnerable to degeneration in the neuropathological context. Furthermore, its ablation was shown to disrupt the hippocampal organization, particularly affecting the lipidome of the dorsal hippocampus (DH) as well as dendritic arborization differentiation in CA1 pyramidal neurons. This specific finding implicates the role of PLD1 in the maintenance of the hippocampal architecture. Given the importance of understanding the cellular context of PLD1 activity in hippocampal neuronal integrity, the need arose to histologically characterize the different glial cell populations within the hippocampus in both the presence and absence of PLD1, as well as the PLD1 processes within them. Ultimately, understanding the relationship between neurons and glial cells — specifically oligodendrocytes and astrocytes — in securing neuronal integrity through the PLD1 pathway would provide valuable insights into the cellular mechanisms underlying hippocampal function. However, previous approaches have not fully captured the extent of PLD1 activity, raising the need for methods that not only quantify PLD1 activity but also localize it at the cellular and subcellular levels. The current study presents the challenges in applying an in-house designed approach based on the IMPACT method, revealing that, while ex vivo 5-hexyn-1ol incubation improved hexynol spatial distribution, non-specific signal in negative controls highlights the need for further technical optimizations. Histological analysis of the CA1 region of the DH implies PLD1 ablation, while not influencing astrocyte and oligodendrocyte cell density, negatively affects their maturation. Additionally, PLD1 ablation appears to disrupt myelination processes in the DH CA1. Further characterization of the morphological structure of both astrocytes and oligodendrocytes would be needed to fully understand the extent of the role PLD1 plays in the differentiation of this cells and, ultimately, on the protection of neuronal integrity.

title: Clinical value of a WNT6-driven Molecular Signature in Glioblastoma Liquid Biopsies
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive malignant primary brain tumor in adults and presents a poor prognosis despite multimodal treatments. Due to its hard-to-reach location, highly invasive nature and striking heterogeneity, GBM is extremely difficult to treat and monitor effectively, resulting in a dismal median overall survival of ~15 months. Current follow-up methods are limited, underscoring the need for complementary monitoring strategies. A promising approach is liquid biopsies, where extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as potential non-invasive biomarkers. WNT ligands are important signaling proteins involved in key processes like cell proliferation and differentiation, that can be transported through EVs. In particular, our team described WNT6 as being associated with GBM aggressiveness and poor prognosis, making it a key target for therapeutic approaches and a promising biomarker. Curiously, WNT6 was previously detected in high levels in GBM cell line-derived EVs. Thus, this work explores the intriguing hypothesis that WNT6 may also be detected in blood EVs and have clinical relevance. In this work, the WNT6 transcriptome, obtained though GBM cell models, revealed enrichment for several EV related processes. In line with this, in GBM patients’ data from TCGA, WNT6-correlated genes also revealed enrichment for vesicle related terms and WNT6 was correlated with EV biogenesis genes. Moreover, our nanoparticle tracking analysis data showed that cells with high WNT6 expression secrete more EVs compared to their low-expressing counterparts. Curiously, we found that GBM patients with WNT6-high tumors also have a higher plasmatic concentration of EVs, further suggesting a link between WNT6 expression and EV release. Impressively, WNT6 was also detected for the first time in EVs isolated from the plasma of several glioma patients, and these EVs mirrored its expression levels in the tumors. This association between tumor and EV expression profiles indicates that WNT6-enriched EVs could provide a reliable, non-invasive snapshot of tumor status. This study provides a foundation for future research aimed at understanding the functional role of WNT6-enriched EVs in GBM. Furthermore, our findings highlight that WNT6 levels in EVs hold substantial potential as prognostic biomarkers for noninvasive liquid biopsies, which may help improve GBM patients’ clinical management.

title: Unravelling the therapeutic efficacy of the multimodal antidepressant vortioxetine in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3
abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia 3 (SCA3) is a polyglutamine neurodegenerative disease characterized by an abnormal CAG repeat expansion within the ATXN3 gene, leading to progressive motor impairments. Currently, there is no available therapy to delay SCA3 progression. Previously, we showed a beneficial impact of serotonin (5-HT) signaling modulation in SCA3 pathology, using either the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor citalopram (CIT) or befiradol, a specific 5-HT1A receptor (5-HT1AR) agonist. Treatment with both compounds significantly alleviated mutant ATXN3-mediated motor defects and neuropathology in SCA3 C. elegans and mouse models. Here, we aimed at testing the safe and clinically approved multimodal antidepressant vortioxetine (VORT) as a novel therapy to mitigate SCA3. Vortioxetine (VORT) is a multimodal antidepressant that acts on several 5-HT elements, operating as a 5-HT transporter blocker, 5-HT1AR agonist, a 5-HT1BR partial agonist and 5-HT1DR, 5-HT3R, and 5-HT7R antagonist. The inhibition of the 5-HT transporter SERT, together with the antagonism of the 5-HT3R potentiates the increase in extracellular 5-HT produced by SERT blockade. This, in combination with the activation of 5-HT1A heteroreceptors and desensitization of autoreceptors responsible for the negative feedback of 5-HT production, would potentially show additional benefit in SCA3 mice. Hence, SCA3 male and female animals were treated chronically with VORT, through food supplementation (10 mg/kg/day). Pre-symptomatic treatment started at 5 weeks of age and lasted 27 weeks. Throughout the experiment animals' health status, neurological signs, and motor behavior performance were tested. Overall, VORT was well tolerated. No differences in food consumption were observed between SCA3 vehicle- and VORT-treated male and female mice. Treatment led to increased body weight, but only in wild-type animals. Regarding motor behavior, VORT did not significantly impact the motor balance and coordination of SCA3 mice, only leading to transient improvements in motor balance performance of SCA3 female mice. Overall, these findings indicate that VORT treatment had a minimal effect on the motor behavior of SCA3 mice. This suggests that modulating serotonergic signaling by targeting multiple 5-HT components simultaneously may not be advantageous for SCA3 under the conditions tested, though the underlying reasons for this remain unclear.

title: Avaliação de um programa de desenvolvimento em preceptoria
abstract: A preceptorship development program consists of a course or set of strategically planned activities to promote the development of health professionals preparing them to play the role of preceptors. Aiming to evaluate the contribution of the “Basic Module” of a preceptorship development program to the training of preceptors in a large hospital in Brazil, this study sought to understand preceptors’ perception of the impact of Preceptorship Development Program - PRODEP o the acquisition of teaching skills. the identification of the potentialities and challenges of a development program aimed at preceptorship and the preceptors’ perception of the impact of the course on their behavior. causing changes in the practice of preceptorship. The evaluation was based on the Kirkpatrick model, which considers four levels: reaction, learning, behavior and results. For this, the research was based on the description of the context and the subjects involved and considering the purposes and characteristics of the topic under study, the research method adopted was of a mixed, qualitative and quantitative nature. The first phase sought to quantify, through structured questionnaires with questions whose answers were on a Likert scale, the participants’ impressions about the course and learning. In the second phase, qualitative methods were used to explore the reasons and meaning of those evaluations and better understand the processes and practices evaluated. The research setting was Hospital Santa Casa de Belo Horizonte and involved professional who completed the PRODEP, in 2019 and 2022, and work in preceptorship of health professional in training. Regarding the data collection procedure, the questionnaire and semi-structured interview were used. To analyze the interviews, we chose to use the content analysis technique, specifically its thematic analysis modality. Three empirical categories emerged from the analysis: “Relevance and methodology of the course”; “Role of educator” and “Change in the practice of preceptorship”. The research concludes that PRODEP positively influenced the practice of preceptors, highlighting the importance of preceptorship development programs in health education.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning to identify assessment needs and to assist faculty decisions
abstract: A educação médica é uma disciplina em constante evolução, onde convergem avanços no conhecimento médico, tecnologia e educação. É por definição altamente permeável a tendências e inovações emergentes. Entre os desenvolvimentos mais transformadores dos últimos anos está a proliferação da inteligência artificial (IA). Esta afeta todos os setores da sociedade, incluindo saúde e educação. Nesta tese, a IA é definida sucintamente, a sua evolução e características-chave. A interseção entre IA e educação médica é central nesta dissertação. É apresentada uma revisão da literatura sobre as inúmeras aplicações das tecnologias associadas à IA em diferentes domínios da educação médica nomeadamente nos mecanismos de avaliação e feedback, plataformas de aprendizagem personalizada, simulações de pacientes virtuais e sistemas de tutoria inteligente. A evidência sugere que a integração de estratégias baseadas em IA produz benefícios tangíveis, facilitando a geração de materiais de ensino, fornecendo feedback eficaz e melhorando o desempenho em níveis educacionais e operacionais. No entanto, apesar das claras vantagens demonstradas por essas tecnologias, sua adoção generalizada nas escolas médicas permanece limitada. Além disso, a IA não é um tópico na maioria dos programas. Essa lacuna deixa estudantes e profissionais de saúde com uma compreensão unilateral da IA, limitando o seu potencial. Abordar essa disparidade é fundamental para garantir que as futuras gerações de alunos e profissionais de saúde estejam equipadas com o conhecimento necessário para navegar em cenários de assistência médica em rápida evolução.

title: Development of quality assessment tools for question construction: utilizing AI models in detecting flaws in item writing
abstract: Introdução: Uma das áreas mais desafiadoras na educação médica é a avaliação. As pergunta de escolha múltipla (PEM) são um dos métodos mais utilizados de avaliação em ambientes educacionais. No entanto, a sua construção é demorada, e a natureza da arquitetura das PEM torna difícil construir itens de teste robustos e confiáveis. O padrão de ouro para o controle de qualidade é a detecção manual dessas falhas, no entanto, este processo é demorado e custoso. Uma ferramenta automatizada eficaz tornaria este processo mais amigável. Novos avanços na inteligência artificial, tanto em acessibilidade quanto em facilidade de uso, tornam possível um caminho para automatizar este processo. Portanto, este projeto visa avaliar a viabilidade e eficácia do uso da Inteligência Artificial (IA) para detectar falhas na elaboração de itens em PEM. Métodos: Para avaliar o GPT-4, usamos uma amostra de 106 itens retirados de um banco de dados já analisado para IWFs. O banco de dados original consiste em 1150 perguntas do Exame Nacional de Seleção português realizado entre 2009 e 2018 e o exame piloto da Prova Nacional de Acesso e foi analisado para IWFs usando critérios estabelecidos e classificações de qualidade (Rush, 2016; Jozefowicz, 2002) utilizando identificação manual. A análise automatizada assistida pelo GPT-4 foi realizada usando otimização de prompt para um grupo de falhas específicas. Resultados: Dos itens analisados, 98,1% tinham pelo menos uma falha. A falha identificada com maior sensibilidade foi em itens de "stems negativas" e "a opção mais longa é a correta". O GPT-4 teve baixa sensibilidade e altas taxas de discordância na identificação dos demais itens. Conclusões: O modelo de IA GPT-4 possui conhecimento intrínseco na construção e validação de questões de múltipla escolha e identificação de falhas na construção, no entanto, apresenta desempenho inferior à revisão humana.
