title: Engineering human Malaria parasites for high-throughput multistage drug screening
abstract: Background: The etiology of malaria involves the infiltration of Plasmodium parasites into the human body, typically transmitted through the bite of female Anopheles mosquitoes. This disease remains a significant global health challenge due to its severe impact and efficient transmission between humans and mosquitoes. In addition, we must consider the emergence of resistance to current first-line treatments, such as artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs), particularly for uncomplicated cases of P. falciparum malaria. Addressing this challenge necessitates the development of innovative and potent drugs. Future therapeutic approaches are envisioned to target not only the symptomatic stage but also the less metabolically active and often neglected gametocyte stage, which is essential for the interruption of the human-to-mosquito transmission. However, a significant obstacle in this pursuit is the scarcity of drugs tailored to this non-symptomatic gametocyte stage, largely due to limitations in mass production and accurate quantification, which hinder high-throughput drug screening efforts. Objectives: Engineer a gametocyte reporter line that can be genetically induced for gametocytogenesis. Moreover, we aim to further improve this line by incorporating fluorescence for streamlined detection of gametocytes. Methodology: Specifically, we employed parasite genome editing methodologies, including the CRISPR-Cas9 system, Bxb1 integrase system, and selection-linked integration (SLI), to build a reporter parasite line using two stage-specific promoters (for asexual and gametocyte) upstream of distinct fluorescent proteins and an inducible system to promote gametocyte commitment. This will facilitate accurate detection and quantification of the two stages through flow cytometry or other imaging-based readouts. Results: Beginning with asexual parasites, a customized pSLI-HP1-GFP-glmS plasmid was engineered to label asexual parasites with GFP through selection-linked integration, along with an inducible glmS system to conditional knockdown of Heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1), the regulator of the AP2-G transcription factor responsible for gametocytogenesis. To generate a gametocyte reporter line, we attempted to introduce a red fluorescent protein-luciferase fusion (EmiRFP670Luc) under a gametocyte-specific promoter (pfs16) using the CRISPR-Cas9 system and/or attP-attB recombinase system. We constructed a customized CRISPR-Cas9 plasmid to insert an attB region into the P. falciparum NF54 strain but were not successful in integrating the EmiRFP670Luc reporter cassette through the Bxb1 integrase system. Subsequently, we attempted the episomal expression of EmiRFP670Luc under the pfs16 promoter but failed to obtain edited parasites. Further investigations are warranted to succeed in this endeavour. Conclusion: Our study underscores the urgent need for novel antimalarial drugs targeting both symptomatic and non-symptomatic stages of the parasite life cycle to effectively interrupt human-to-mosquito transmission. Despite encountering challenges in constructing a gametocyte reporter line, our innovative approach - using parasite genome editing - methodologies has laid the groundwork for accurate detection and quantification of asexual and gametocyte stages. While initial attempts to introduce the EmiRFP670Luc reporter cassette were unsuccessful, further investigations are warranted to overcome these obstacles and advance toward developing effective therapies against malaria.

title: Noradrenergic degeneration in a DJ-1 knockout mouse model
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder, with approximately 10% familial cases, caused by several identified mutations, such as in the DJ-1 gene. DJ-1 knockout (KO) mouse models have been shown to present progressive motor behavioral deficits, without significant alterations in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, described as the neuropathological substrate of PD. Degeneration of the noradrenergic nucleus - locus coeruleus (LC) - has been linked to the development of non-motor symptoms and to the aggravation of motor symptoms. Herein, we aimed to study the involvement of LC degeneration in a DJ-1 KO model looking at both motor and non-motor phenotype. For that, we have administered a selective noradrenergic neurotoxin (DSP-4) in DJ-1 KO mice. First, we optimized the appropriate dosage to be administered. To assess functional alterations, we have performed a battery of behavioral tests covering several symptoms associated with PD, including depression, anxiety, cognitive impairments, impaired locomotor activity and gait dysfunction. To assess the histological effects of both DSP-4 and the mutation we have performed Tyrosine Hydroxylase (TH) immunohistochemistry on the LC, substantia nigra (SNpc), and striatum (STR). DJ-1 animals have shown tendencies to impaired motor functioning, gait dysfunction and a tendency to develop anxiety-related to novelty. DJ-1 KO treated with DSP-4 showed impaired swimming ability, gait dysfunction, tendency for depressive-like behavior, and improved fear memory retrieval. DJ-1 animals showed a reduction of 42.6% in striatal densitometry and a decrease in the number of TH+ cells in the SNpc compared to WT littermates. The injection of DSP-4 led to a decrease of 83-85% neurons within the LC. DSP-4 administration in DJ-1 mice led to a 58% decrease in dopaminergic fibers content in the striatum but did not affect nigral neurons. In this work, we developed a model capable of recapitulating noradrenergic degeneration described in PD, which led to significant nigrostriatal degeneration, and was translated into mild behavioral phenotype, at the motor and non-motor level. This model may provide a suitable approach for the study of neuroprotective therapies focused on the LC noradrenergic neurons.

title: Dissecting the role of immunometabolism in granuloma formation in sarcoidosis
abstract: Sarcoidosis is a granulomatous condition with unknown etiology that predominantly affects the lungs. This disorder is characterized by the formation of granulomas resulting from the accumulation of immune cells and an inadequate resolution of inflammation. Cell metabolism is a crucial mechanism whereby immune cells modulate their function. Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) is the rate-limiting enzyme of tryptophan metabolism and displays a fundamental immunoregulatory role, crucial at the interface between inflammation and cell immunity. Our data revealed that, among the genes involved in cellular metabolism, expression of Ido1 gene was upregulated during granuloma formation in experimental sarcoid granulomas. On the other hand, the products of L-tryptophan oxidation by IDO1, known as L-kynurenines, have been described as having tolerogenic functions, such as T regulatory cell activation and anti-inflammatory cytokine production. We hypothesize that IDO1 represents an essential modulatory element in sarcoidosis by regulating immune cell mobilization and granuloma formation and, as a result, influences the progression and the outcome of the disease. In this work, we took advantage of an in vivo model of sarcoid granuloma using wild-type and Ido1 knockout mice. Our work shows that Ido1 deficiency disturbs the early phase of granuloma formation, as well as cytokine production and immune cell distribution. In patients, we showed that the rs7820268 genetic variant that underlies IDO1 deficiency may dictate the severity and the outcome of the disease. These results contribute to an improved understanding of the molecular mechanisms that underlie granulomatous inflammation and to the potential development of novel therapeutic interventions for sarcoidosis.

title: Implantação de EPAs no internato de Pediatria de um curso de medicina no Brasil
abstract: The present study explores the implementation of Entrustable Professional Activities (EPA) in Pediatrics clerkship of a Brazilian medical school in a formal-embranced and competency-based curriculum basis. The primary aim is developing and validating a specific EPAs for future implementation. EPAs were created in 2005 as an educational tool for competency longitudinal assessment and is widely used in professional practice already. Initially created for being appplied in Medical Residency, it has more recently also been used in undergraduate medical education, including in Brazil, where its use is still in the very beginning phases. The study has involved the initial development of EPA after an extensive literature reviewing and their subsequent validation through a consensus of experts using the modified Delphi technique. Expert’s written contributions were evaluated through thematic content analysis and descriptive statistical analysis. Seven EPAs were developed and validated after a process that resulted in a strong consensus and a high rate of Cumulative Agreement index after two rounds of experts interactions. The achieved results have been as similar as others previewed reports in EPAs tools application in undergraduate medical education, also opening up an innovative contribution of this project in the development of specific EPA for the Pediatrics specialty clerkship, highlighting the relevance and applicability of EPAs in clinical context. The future implementation of the validation achieved in a Brazilian medical school Pediatrics clerkship is the next step. It is expected that the present EPAs model can be applied several of medical schools in Brazil in order to improve assessment processes in competency-based medical education.

title: Development and implementation of Entrustable Professional Activities in Portuguese Anesthesia Residency Program – a pilot study
abstract: Introduction: In the last decades postgraduate medical education is changing to a competence-based system centred on outcome. The Entrustable Professional Activities (EPA) are a “units of work” that can be done, observed, and assessed and are aligned with the new educational paradigm. Portuguese anesthesia residency training does not include a competence-based curriculum, and in this domain has residual workplace-based assessment. This pilot study wants to promote the development and the implementation of EPA in Portuguese anesthesia residency programs. The present study aimed to (1) characterize Portuguese stakeholder’s interest on EPA; (2) promote faculty development on Competence- Based Medical Education (CBME) concept; (3) develop one pilot EPA and (4) implement and assess the pilot EPA in a small group of Portuguese hospitals. Methods: (1) A survey was distributed to the Portuguese Anesthesia Community. Demographic characterization; interest and familiarity with EPAs; sources of knowledge; interest in improving knowledge on the field as well as motivation to be enrolled in implementation process, were surveyed. (2) Faculty development initiatives were created as presential meetings and online e-learning sessions. (3) A pilot EPA was developed after focus group discussions. (4) The pilot EPA was implemented through workplace-based assessment, using a mobile application. Questionnaires to evaluate the experience and the usability of the application will be sent and analyzed. Results: (1) 142 participants answered the initial survey. Among the participants, 53% were residents and 42% were consultants with 10-20 years of experience. 61% of participants were not familiar with the concept of EPA; 98% wanted to improve their knowledge on EPA; 93% found it relevant to initiate EPA implementation, and 92% wished to be enrolled in the process. (2) 6 faculty development initiatives meetings were conducted in 5 hospitals. A total of 167 consultants and 51 residents were invited. (3) Induction of Anesthesia for ASA I/II fasting patient with no difficult airway for a low-risk procedure, was the pilot EPA developed. (4) The pilot EPA was implemented in 5 hospitals, and its assessment was done using mobile the preparedEPA application. Conclusions: The implementation of EPA in Portuguese anesthesia residency programs is feasible. Residents and consultants should be recruited for the implementation process. The first step should focus on faculty development.

title: Motivando mentes médicas: adaptação da Escala de Motivação Académica no âmbito da Teoria da Autodeterminação
abstract: Introduction: Motivation plays a crucial role in the academic success and professional development of medical students. Understanding the intricacies of motivation within the context of medical education is essential for designing effective interventions and support systems. This paper explores the adaptation of the Academic Motivation Scale (AMS) within the framework of Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and of Self-efficacy Theory to assess motivation among medical students. Methods: The study utilized a rigorous methodology to adapt the AMS to the Portuguese context, drawing upon insights from SDT. Two existing Portuguese scales, MATAMS and Ribeiro et al.'s scale, served as foundational frameworks for the adaptation process. The resulting Minho Medical Academic Motivation Scale (Minho-MEDAMS) underwent thorough validation procedures to ensure its psychometric properties and validity. Results: The adaptation process yielded a refined scale comprising five dimensions of motivation: intrinsic motivation, identified regulation, external regulation, introjected regulation, and amotivation. Psychometric analyses demonstrated strong reliability and validity of the Minho-MEDAMS, affirming its suitability for assessing motivation among medical students in the Portuguese context. Discussion and Conclusion: The successful adaptation of the AMS within the SDT framework presents a valuable instrument for assessing motivation in medical students. The Minho-MEDAMS offers a comprehensive understanding of motivational dynamics, facilitating targeted interventions and support mechanisms to enhance student engagement and success. Its validity and reliability render it a practical tool for educators, administrators, and researchers in the field of medical education. Ultimately, the Minho-MEDAMS contributes to the advancement of strategies aimed at cultivating motivated and proficient healthcare professionals.

title: Escala de Avaliação de Sutura do Minho - Desenvolvimento e validação
abstract: Objective: This research introduces and validates the Minho Suture Assessment Scale (Minho- SAS), a comprehensive tool designed for the evaluation of fundamental suturing competencies in medical students. Employing Item Response Theory (IRT) and a dichotomous yes/no response format, the scale provides a detailed framework for assessing suturing abilities. Methods: The development process involved collaboration with multidisciplinary teams and experienced practitioners to develop the Minho-SAS and to ensure content validity. Validation methods incorporated IRT techniques, utilizing the Rasch model and the 2-PL model to assess reliability, construct validity, and measurement precision. Rigorous psychometric evaluation was conducted using data from a cohort of 5th-year medical students. Results: The final Minho-SAS consisted of 15 dichotomic yes/no items and exhibited robust internal consistency, reliability, and construct validity across both Rasch and 2-PL models. Item analyses revealed insights into individual item performance, elucidating varying levels of difficulty and discrimination among the 15 assessment components. The scale's emphasis on fundamental suturing skills was evident in its detailed evaluation, setting it apart from broader assessment tools. Conclusion: The Minho-SAS proves to be a promising instrument specifically tailored for assessing fundamental suturing skills in medical students. Its rigorous validation through IRT methodologies underscores its precision and reliability, positioning it as a valuable addition to existing evaluation scales. While showing considerable promise, further exploration across diverse populations and educational settings is essential to confirm its broader applicability and impact in medical education and clinical practice.

title: Development and implementation of a digital portfolio in fundamental sciences
abstract: Introdução: A necessidade de repensar o médico no futuro, levou a uma expansão no uso de portfólios na educação de profissionais de saúde (1,2). Devido à grande variedade de tipos de portfólio torna impossível fazer uma observação geral sobre eles. No entanto, e apesar das suas muitas variações, podemos dividi-los em dois tipos principais: o portfólio reflexivo e portfólios mais abrangentes (3,4). Ambos os tipos visam apoiar o processo de aprendizagem dos alunos e avaliar o seu progresso. Métodos: Na Escola Médica da UMinho implementámos em 2021, a utilização do portefólio no 1º e 2º ano do currículo onde os alunos estão a ter formação em Ciências Básicas. Foi implementado um portfólio que contem 3 componentes: 1) Indicadores Pedagógicos, 2) Atividades extracurriculares relevantes para o desenvolvimento profissional e 3) Componente Reflexiva. Pretendeu-se que o aluno fosse capaz de acompanhar a sua evolução, de forma crítica e reflexiva, com o objetivo final de promover uma atitude proativa na aprendizagem individual. Analisamos as notas obtidas no portfólio, pelos alunos do 1º e do 2º ano, usando para isso os resultados da coorte de 21-22 e 22-23. Resultados: Observamos que não há diferença nas notas da componente 2 entre os alunos do 1º e do 2º ano na primeira coorte, mas na segunda observamos que os alunos do 2º ano tinham melhores notas. Vimos ainda que os alunos do 2º ano, em ambas as coortes tinham melhor desempenho na componente 3. Mostramos que, embora as componentes 2 e 3 tenham sido reconhecidas como relevantes, a componente 1 não foi útil no sentido de que é um registro das classificações obtidas na Componente de conhecimentos (avaliações sumativas) e na Componente de Competências e Atitudes. Conclusão: Sendo este um portfólio de ciência básica, propomos alterar a componente 1 e introduzir, para as aulas laboratoriais, um e-book onde os alunos, para cada aula, registram o objetivo da aula; metodologias usadas para atingir esse objetivo; os resultados; breve discussão sobre como a metodologia foi útil para atingir o objetivo e uma breve reflexão sobre o que aprenderam e como se sentiram na execução daquela habilidade técnica/metodologia. Pretendemos ainda ter atividades como preparação e submissão de pósteres científicos, jornal clubs, redação de cartas a editores e discussão de casos que envolvam questões relacionadas à integridade e ética científica. No futuro deverá também ser abordado o impacto da introdução deste novo formato de portfólio na aprendizagem e desenvolvimento de uma atitude critica e proativa do aluno.
authors: Marques, Fernanda Cristina Gomes de Sousa

title: Implantação da telemedicina como prática médica no currículo de graduação
abstract: The present study aims to implement telemedicine as practical training in the undergraduate medical curriculum at two higher education institutions, one in Belo Horizonte (UNIBH) and the other in the metropolitan region (FASEH) of Vespasiano, Minas Gerais, Brazil, in the clinical and internship cycles through the use of the ProntLife platform. This is a descriptive study of a mixed nature, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches, conducted at two medical schools within the Inspirali group. Data were extracted from ProntLife and analyzed using thematic content analysis. Additionally, a literature review was conducted using PUBMED, LILACS, and SCIELO databases, with descriptors used to search for articles on the use of telemedicine in medical education, the history of telemedicine and its implementation, telemedicine regulations in Brazil, and a brief contextualization of Inspirali. The review also covered the use of telemedicine during the Covid-19 pandemic in Brazil, the description of the setup of telemedicine services in the medical course of a higher education institution in Belo Horizonte, and discussions on the implementation with faculty members. Collaboratively, with the Innovation Directorate of Inspirali, the study explored telemedicine as a simulation. Through the implementation of this project, the goal is to incorporate telemedicine as a practice in simulations and outpatient clinics in the undergraduate medical curriculum. The study aims to evaluate the effects of integrating telemedicine into medical education and its impact on access to healthcare for vulnerable groups. Furthermore, it intends to assess the impacts on healthcare services that are engaged in this practice with the medical school.

title: Implicações da comunidade de prática no raciocínio moral e ético: estudo de caso
abstract: Introduction: Clinical Ethics is a crucial factor to professionalism and good clinical practice. Compliance to ethical principles must be reached and maintained throughout the medical career. However, evidence suggests the existence of ethical erosion, probably due to the effects of a hidden curriculum. Some sort of intervention becomes necessary to counter that phenomenon. According to the most recent perspectives, a training program in Clinical Ethics shall use active learning strategies, with discussion of real clinical cases between colleagues, in a clear correspondence to the learning theory “Community of Practice”. Objectives: Estimate the existence of ethical erosion in a certain medical community; Create a modern training program in Clinical Ethics; Evaluate the impact of the community in its members’ ethical reasoning; Evaluate participants’ satisfaction and benefits of a training program to the community. Methods: The Defining Issues Test (DIT-2) was delivered to the doctors of the Internal Medicine department, Braga Hospital. A small group also started a training program in Clinical Ethics whose impact was evaluated at individual and collective levels through the application of questionnaires in each session and at the end of the program. Data was analysed through quantitative and qualitative methods. Results: Data analysis from the DIT-2 test showed that there is a significant weak negative correlation between age and N2 score. Also, younger practitioners (≤ 35 years of age) have significantly better scores in the test than older doctors. On the other task, participants expressed a very high level of satisfaction with the program in terms of methodology used, mode, practicality, applicability and perceived individual and collective impact. Participants believe that this kind of programs strengthens the community of practice and its pillars: connection, belonging, shared values and alignment. On the other hand, by analysing the answers to the questionnaires delivered at the end of each session, it became very clear the great impact of the community of practice in its members’ ethical reasoning or judgment. Conclusion: Ethical erosion seems to exist in the studied community. The high impact of the community of practice in its members, makes it mandatory that future pedagogic interventions in the field of Clinical Ethics are directed to the community instead of single individuals.

title: Atividades Profissionais Confiáveis (APCs) como estratégia para o desenvolvimento curricular do internato em saúde mental do curso de medicina da UniMAX: contribuições para a formação do médico generalista
abstract: The current National Curriculum Guidelines for undergraduate medical courses in Brazil were published in 2014. This document proposes that the curricular structure of the courses be competency-based and include, for the first time, mental health as one of the mandatory areas during the internship programmes. The definition of educational goals for the internship in mental health, the provision of educational environment and the learning assessment strategies for this programme are each medical school’s responsibility. The increase in the prevalence and severity of mental disorders in the population imposes new challenges for the future general practitioner’s education and its practice in mental health care. This research aimed to identify the necessary elements for the elaboration and subsequent validation of EPAs as curricular development strategy of the internship programme in mental health of the medical school at UniMAX. EPAs have been widely used to better translate Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) into clinical practice. EPAs are defined as units of professional practice that can be performed, observed, and entrusted to a student as soon as they demonstrate competency to perform it safely. Methodology: This is a descriptive study, with an exploratory approach that used primary information for its development. A previously prepared form was sent to 46 members of the local academic community. The responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Likert scale, and content analysis. Results: The elements necessary for using the EPAs are known to the participants: learning assessment tools, with emphasis on 360-degree appraisal and feedback. and the descriptive components used in the course's pedagogical project’s competency profile are also known. Professional activities associated with psychiatry obtained the lowest agreement rates on the Likert scale for composing the educational objectives for the mental health internship program.

title: GABA, a potential immunomodulator in spinal cord injury
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a severe neurological condition that results in the loss of motor and sensory function below the injury site, disrupting communication between the brain and the rest of the body. This results in several comorbidities that significantly reduce patients’ quality of life. Currently, there is no effective therapy available for SCI, making research in this field crucial. SCI has a complex pathophysiology that can be divided into two phases. The first phase involves mechanical damage caused by the trauma (primary injury), followed by a cascade of molecular and cellular events that damage otherwise intact tissue (secondary injury). This secondary injury leads to further dysfunction, restricting functional recovery. In mammals, SCI causes permanent tissue loss characterized by a chronic state of neuroinflammation. Baclofen is a GABA agonist widely used to manage spasticity, being frequently employed in chronic SCI patients for this purpose. Recent studies suggest that baclofen may have direct therapeutic effects in SCI. It has been demonstrated to promote both functional recovery and neuroprotection and suggested to modulate the immune response in this context. In the present study, we aimed to explore the immunomodulation properties of baclofen. Two main approaches were used to pursue this goal: (1) create an in vitro system that mimics SCI for further in-depth studies in this research framework; (2) evaluate the acute administration effects of different baclofen doses (1 and 5 mg/kg) in the immune response early-on after injury, using a well-established murine in vivo compression SCI model. Regarding the SCI in vitro system, our research indicates that additional investigation is necessary to uncover the molecular mechanisms affected by baclofen in a neural context following SCI. In the in vivo study, we strategically selected timepoints that correspond to peaks in immune cell infiltration at lesion core. Data shows that baclofen facilitates a regulated immune response post-SCI, which potentially lays the groundwork for observed functional recovery. Notably, our studies indicates that 1 mg/Kg dose of baclofen significantly modulates the immune response at local, systemic, and peripheric levels. This finding raises the need for further studies to determine if the immune response modulation is casually linked to the observed improvements in locomotor outcomes among baclofen-treated animals. In conclusion, our study provides new evidence that baclofen can modulate the immune response following SCI. This position baclofen as a noteworthy drug in the realm of immunomodulators, paving the way for further exploration of its therapeutic potential.

title: Impact of early inflammatory events in vaccine-induced protection against Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection
abstract: Tuberculosis, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of death due to a single infectious agente. The Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine represents a pivotal strategy in the global fight against tuberculosis; however, it presents a variable efficacy. Alveolar macrophages are the first immune cells to interact with M. tuberculosis when it reaches the lower airways and serve as a vehicle to transport bacteria from the alveolar space to the lung paremchyma, leading to the initiation of several innate and adaptive immune responses. We have previously observed that alveolar macrophages from the susceptible mice C3HeB/FeJ retain intracellular bacteria for longer periods when compared to C57BL/6 mice, which are more resistant to infection. Considering that BCC-induced response is dependent on CD4- T cells response, here we sought to determine how thew early inflammatory events of the immune response against M. tuberculosis to impact the protection induced by vaccination. Our data demonstrate that the location of M tuberculosis in alveolar macrophages can impact the protection conferred by BCC vaccination. Specifically, we found an association between the location of M. tuberculosis in alveolar macrophages with a delayed vaccine-induced immune response upon infection. Still, BCG vaccination anticipated the immune response against M. tuberculosis infection. In fact, vaccinated mice demonstrated an earlier dissemination of M. tuberculosis from alveolar macrophages to other myeloid cells in the lung parenchyma, and an earlier activation and accumulation of CD4- T cells in the lungs. As a result, vaccinated susceptible mice demonstrated an improved control of M. tuberculosis in the lungs. Importantly, this control was similar to that observed in non-vaccinated resistant mice, but only at 30 days post-infecton. Therefore, these findings suggest that BCG vaccination can partially compensate for the delay observed in bacterial dissemination from alveolar macrophages in C3HeB/FeJ mice. Future studies will investigate the long-lasting response to BCG regarding the susceptibility and resistance to M. tuberculosis.

title: Sex differences in the sympathetic regulation of the immune response and functional recovery after Spinal Cord Injury
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) leads to progressive immune system dysfunction and triggers a local pro-inflammatory response with non-resolving attributes. Sympathetic nervous system circuits are critically involved in regulating the immune response through signalling to lymphoid organs. Our research group has been studying how SCI impacts this neuroimmune regulation, with a particular focus on the disruption of the sympathetic circuit between the spinal cord and the spleen, and the potential of this organ as a target for immunomodulation of SCI-associated inflammation. However, as with most SCI research, these studies were conducted only on female rodent models. Given the known sexual dimorphism of the autonomic and immune systems, this project aims to dissect sex-differences in sympathetic regulation of the immune response following SCI, with the goal of understanding the sex-specific influence of sympathetic signalling on SCI recovery. To this end, we aim to study the impact of splenic denervation in both sexes on acute and chronic immune responses and on long-term recovery of motor, sensory, and autonomic functions, by performing flow cytometry and several behavioural analyses. Our results demonstrated that sympathetic signalling regulates the myeloid cells infiltration into the spinal cord of males, leading to a delayed inflammatory response during the acute phase of injury. During this phase, females display a combination of a pro-inflammatory activation profile − also observed in males − and a reparative profile, which is absent in males. However, cells with reparative phenotypes in females vanishes at the chronic phase. Overall, at the chronic phase of SCI, neither sex nor sympathetic signalling exerts relevant effects on cellular activation profiles, correlating with the lack of these effects on functional recovery. In conclusion, we demonstrated the existence of sex-differences in several aspects of the immune response following SCI, some dependent and others independent on sympathetic signalling, highlighting that both factors influence this immune response. Thus, this dissertation emphasizes the need to include both sexes in future studies focusing on understanding the precise mechanisms by which SCI affects the neuronal regulation of the immune response, ultimately guiding the development of personalized therapies that account for sex-specific pathophysiological variations while aiming to restore immune system homeostasis.

title: Compound library screening for neural repair: finding new drugs for old problems
abstract: Traumatic central nervous system (CNS) injuries, including traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI), lead to severe and often irreversible physical, cognitive, and psychological impairments. Despite ongoing research, no effective therapeutic strategies have been developed to address the complex pathophysiological and inhibitory microenvironments that restrain neuroplasticity and tissue repair. In this study, we aimed to explore novel therapeutic approaches by screening a recently synthesized compound library for its neural repair capabilities. This library was screened in cortex and spinal cord cell cultures derived from rats, employing the MTS assay to identify compound-induced metabolic alterations. This initial screening led to the identification of seven promising compounds (ST1059, ST1055, ST673, ST656, ST149, ST666, and ST18). Further characterization using immunocytochemistry revealed that three of these compounds promoted enhanced oligodendrocyte branching, suggesting possible potentiation of remyelination. Additionally, three compounds where able to induce significant increases in microglia area which can indicate possible immune activation. Molecular analysis of our cultures did not reveal significant changes in the mRNA expression levels of genes associated with oligodendrocyte maturation, though there was a trend towards increased expression of oligodendrocyte progenitor markers. Analysis of the Rho/ROCK signaling pathway, known to play an important role in CNS injury and repair, did not show alterations in RhoA mRNA expression, however, one compound significantly upregulated ROCK1 mRNA expression. In summary, this study identified three compounds that promote oligodendrocyte branching, which may enhance myelination and provide structural and functional support to neurons. These findings suggest that these compounds may possess neuroregenerative properties, however more studies are needed to understand their real therapeutic value.

title: Impact and transcriptomic analysis of the effect of the Secretome of Adipose Tissue derived Stem Cells in an in vitro Model of Spinal Cord Injury
abstract: Spinal Cord Injury (SCI) is a consequence of the physical damage directly to the spinal cord or to the tissues surrounding it, leading to temporary or permanent alterations in sensory and motor functions. Arising from this, an instant neuronal death prolonged by a combination of neurodegenerative events lead to a poor outcome and failure of therapeutic attempts. Regenerative medicine-based approaches have been bringing more attention as promising therapies for SCI, specifically cell-free based therapies. Preliminary studies have shown the therapeutic benefits of the use of Adipose tissue derived stem cells (ASCs) secretome in a SCI context, where significant improvements in motor tests and axonal growth were reported. Despite these observations, there is still missing the underlying molecular mechanism for these improvements. Thus, the aim of this work was to characterize the ASCs secretome capacity in modulating signaling pathways in a pre-characterized in vitro model of spinal cord, subjected to a chemical insult. For this, a secretome dose-effect was determined through cell viability and by analyzing changes in the different population present in the chosen model through fluorescence microscopy. This work findings suggest that concentration at 1x has the most relevant outcomes, by significantly enhancing cell survival and promoting neuronal protection. No conclusions could be taken from microglia and astrocytes responses, indicating a need for further investigation of these populations. Hence, the molecular characterization proceeded with ASCs secretome at 1x, through a transcriptomic profiling of the signaling pathways using RNA-Seq analysis. Significant functional enrichments were found after treatment, related to an up-regulation of cell cycle pathways and, on the other hand, a down-regulation correlated to oxidative phosphorylation functions. In addition of reenforcing the use of the ASCs secretome as a therapy for SCI, these results could possibly lead to future advances in this approach by enhancement of its potential.

title: The role of astrocytic Foxo1 in the dorsal hippocampus
abstract: Astrocytes have emerged as critical players in cognitive functions, namely in memory and learning, which are hippocampus-dependent functions. In previous studies of the host laboratory, the IP₃R2 KO mouse model was used to study calcium signaling in astrocytes in this brain region. A transcriptomic analysis of hippocampal tissue from IP₃R2 KO mice revealed that 677 genes were differentially expressed, from which 349 were up-regulated and 328 were down-regulated. A bioinformatic analysis identified 9 transcription factors linked to the regulatory sequences associated with the differentially expressed genes. Among them, the Forkheacl Box 01 (Foxo1) was enriched in astrocytes and regulated 76 of the 677 genes. Of these, 5 genes were significantly upregulated, including Syndecan-2 and Ezrin, which are important for synaptic structure. Structural analysis of pyramidal neurons from the dorsal hippocampus (dHIP) of IP₃R2 KO mice showed that neurons presented a normal morphology while displaying a shift in neuronal spine profile from mature to immature spines, which plays important roles in the formation and maintenance of a functional neural circuitry and memory processes. Furthermore, we found that these IP₃R2 KO mice display an enhancement of long-term fear memory. To confirm a causal relationship between these molecular, structural, and behavioral observations, we used a viral approach to induce the overexpression of Foxo1 in hippocampal astrocytes in C57BL/6J mice. The overexpression recapitulated the structural, synaptic, and behavioral changes observed in IP₃R2 KO mice. Therefore, this dissertation aimed to confirm whether Foxo1-dependent gene transcription is necessary for physiological astrocytic structure, spine morphology, and behavior. To achieve this, we used a viral approach to silence Foxo1, specifically in astrocytes of the dHIP of C57BL/6J mice. Mice with Foxo1 silenced in dHIP astrocytes were characterized at the behavioral, molecular, and structural levels. Behavioral analyses revealed that Foxo1 silencing in hippocampal astrocytes enhances immediate spatial and long-term recognition memories. Furthermore, the 3D reconstruction of astrocyte morphology revealed that Foxo1 silencing in hippocampal astrocytes increases the number of processes and morphological complexity. Finally, silencing of astrocytic Foxo1, leads to the increase of spine density in CA1 pyramidal neurons within the dHIP. These studies contributed to discovering a novel role of the astrocytic Foxo1 transcription factor in shaping hippocampal circuit structure and hippocampal-dependent memory.

title: Genomic profiling of gastrointestinal stromal tumours using whole-exome sequencing
abstract: Os tumores estromais gastrointestinais (GIST) são raros, no entanto constituem as neoplasias mesenquimatosas mais comuns do trato gastrointestinal, afetando maioritariamente o estômago e o intestino delgado. Apesar da maioria dos GISTs ter alterações nos protooncogenes KIT e PDGFRA, 15% são considerados GISTs de tipo selvagem. Os GISTs com alteração no KIT e PDGFRA são mais sensíveis a inibidores de tirosina quinase (TKIs) do que o tipo selvagem, ressaltando a urgência de estudar o perfil genómico dos GIST. As abordagens com sequenciamento de nova geração (NGS) são cruciais para a oncologia de precisão e investigação de terapias dirigidas. A análise de dados gerados no sequenciamento do exoma exige experiência em bioinformática. Existem vários desafios nesta análise, incluindo a necessidade de curadoria manual, a inexistência de uma pipeline universal e a variabilidade inerente entre ferramentas bem consolidadas. Independentemente dos desafios, a bioinformática tem um papel crucial na genómica do cancro. Esta dissertação teve o objetivo de identificar o perfil genómico de 19 pacientes de GIST, usando WES de tumor/sangue, e associar o perfil molecular com as suas características clínicas. A idade da população estudada variou entre os 44 e os 76 anos. A localização do tumor primário mais comum foi o estômago, seguida do intestino delgado. O conjunto inicial de variantes somáticas foi de 10.981 e, através da aplicação de filtros, foram identificadas 212 com potencial de patogenicidade. Após a classificação das variantes por três abordagens diferentes, foram encontradas 31 com evidência de patogenicidade. Os genes KIT e PDGFRA continuaram a ser os genes mais alterados, embora tenham sido identificados outros genes sem relação com cancro em pacientes com alteração no KIT. Foi identificado um caso de GIST de tipo selvagem com uma variante no gene EGFR, sugerindo o envolvimento deste gene nesta doença. A taxa de sobrevivência de 5 anos foi de 89.5%. Pacientes com risco de malignidade de Fletcher elevado demonstraram menor probabilidade de sobrevivência. GISTs com alterações no KIT demonstraram uma taxa de sobrevivência de 5 anos de 86.7%, enquanto que os pacientes com alterações no gene PDGFRA apresentaram uma sobrevivência global mais elevada. Este estudo forneceu informações interessantes acerca do panorama genético específico de GIST de uma população brasileira.

title: Defining dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine resistance pathways in the malaria parasite
abstract: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) isthe current first-line treatment for uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. In this 3-day treatment, a highly efficient yet fast-acting artemisinin derivative is combined with a slow-acting and functionally distinct partner- drug to clear out the remaining parasites. One of these combinations is dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA-PPQ), commonly deployed in Southeast Asia. Similarly to other antimalarials, tolerance has developed for this combination, threatening both the control and prophylaxis of this disease in this region. There are also increasing concerns regarding the spread of this tolerance to Africa, where 96% of malaria deaths take place. On a molecular level, artemisinin tolerance is associated with single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Plasmodium falciparum’s pfk13 gene, which encodes for the K13 protein, an ubiquitin signaling protein involved in the regulation of a multitude of pathways such as endocytosis and cellular trafficking of host hemoglobin. Among other effects, these mutations have shown to decrease hemoglobin uptake by the parasite. Because artemisinins rely on free heme generated during hemoglobin degradation (as a source of nutrients for the parasite) for their activation, these mutants experience reduced drug activation, which consequently decreases treatment effectiveness. Piperaquine tolerance is associated with an increased gene copy number of pfpm2, encoding for plasmepsins II, aspartic proteases involved in hemoglobin degradation. The overexpression of pfpm2 might alleviate the fitness cost associated with hemoglobin degradation resulting from K13 mutations. The combination of pfpm2 copy number with K13 SNPs has been found in clinical isolates, however, the exact mechanism and implications underlying this combination are still unclear. To gain deeper insights into these molecular markers of resistance and explore the potential interaction between them in enhancing the parasite’s drug response under selective drug pressure, we designed and employed the CRISPR-Cas9 system as a genetic engineering tool. Our objective was to generate recombinant parasite lines that combine pfk13 SNPs and pfpm2 duplications. However, we encountered several challenges during the generation of these recombinants and explored various troubleshooting options. The output of the analysis of drug response, hemoglobin catabolism and fitness cost can lead to the unveiling of the complex crosstalk among DHA and PPQ resistant factors and the molecular basis of multi-drug resistance.

title: Interneuron characterization in Rett Syndrome: insights from mice prefrontal cortex
abstract: The Prefrontal cortex (PFC) is the brain region responsible for higher-order cognitive and executive functions. The medial PFC is the subregion that plays a crucial role in enabling essential tasks necessary for human thinking. The region is composed of cytoarchitecture and functionally distinct areas, in which at the single neuron level and each cortical network are controlled by excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) inputs that establish a dynamic ratio fundamental to maintain proper brain activity. Disbalance in E/I network has been associated with neurobehavioral syndromes and autistic-like features. Rett Syndrome (RTT) is a neurodevelopment disorder affecting mostly females. It is inherited in an X-linked manner and caused by the loss of function of methyl-Cp G binding protein 2 (MeCP2), encoded by the MECP2 gene. Previous research has shown that MeCP2 plays diverse roles in different brain regions and contributes to cognitive and social functions. Moreover, MeCP2 expression seems to have a class-specific effect upon which some types of interneurons (IN) are more affected than others by the absence of the gene. Despite being a disorder with severe cognitive impairments and well-defined sex distribution, most RTT studies disregard phenotypic characterization in female mice as well as the alterations of the cortical network in the PFC, which, as stated, is a region with a central role in cognition. Our primary aim was to assess alterations of distinct cortical IN expressing parvalbumin (PV+) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP+) within the PFC, with a particular focus on female heterozygous mice Mecp2 tm1.1Bird mice —a widely accepted model of RTT by immunofluorescence assay and a semi-automated 2D fluorescence-based workflows for analysis. Our findings at the 12-week-old mark revealed a trend towards reduced PV immunoreactivity in female Mecp2 +/- mice, especially pronounced in the dorsomedial PFC (dmPFC) and infralimbic cortex (IL). Additionally, we also observed decreased expression of VIP in MeCP2 null cells in Mecp2 +/- mice, suggesting a potential link between loss of MeCP2. These differences may underlie the phenotype seen in Mecp2 +/- mice, which often exhibit motor impairments and breathing disturbances, as well as support the class-specific effect of MeCP2 expression in cortical IN. Overall, cortical IN may play an important role in the pathogenesis of Rett Syndrome, leading to potential over-inhibition of specific cortical networks in crucial regions involved in motor and cognitive process. This elucidation is a crucial step toward understanding the cellular components of MeCP2 deficiency and, consequently, identifying novel pharmacological targets.

title: Electrically stimulated neural stem cells encapsulated in gellan gum hydrogel for spinal cord injury repair
abstract: Spinal Cord Injuries (SCI) can have a devastating impact on an individual’s life, leadind to motor, sensory, psychological and social impairments. The SCI pathophysiology associated is extremely complex, with numerous molecular and cellular events occurring after the initial trauma and that lead to the development of an inhibitory microenvironment in the injury site, which impairs the development of new therapies. Therefore, therapies that combine different strategies have been on the rise for focusing on different critical events. For instance, several types of cells have been implanted in order to replace lost tissue after these types of lesions. Induced Neural Stem Cells (iNSCs) have been the most promising for autologous transplant and differentiation in neurons, astrocytes and oligodendrocytes. To promote the survival of transplanted cells, biomaterials have been implemented to act as an artificial extracelullar matrix. Additionally, some pathological events and, as a consequence, the success of the transplanted cells, can be enhanced using the secretome of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). At last, epidural electrical stimulation has revealed to be a promising therapy for SCI, enabling physical rehabilitation and promoting neural plasticity. Therefore, this project aims to combine all this approaches in order to target several pathophysiolgical events of the spinal cord injury, instead of just one. As a result, we perform in vitro studies on the combination of stem cells, biomaterials, secretome and epidural electrical stimulation in order to obtain an effective therapy.
authors: Armada, Miguel João Loureiro Afonso da Rocha

title: Novel phenotypic features of the malaria parasite through time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance
abstract: Malaria infections remain a scourge in endemic regions worldwide, stalling economic growth and reducing life expectancyin children. The path towards malaria control and elimination has been hindered by drug resistance and ineffective diagnostic tools to detect low density and asymptomatic infections. With the limited portfolio of drugs available to treat malaria, it is fundamental to improve the understanding of resistance mechanisms and appraise parasite cell biology and pathogenesis. In this dissertation, we aimed to exploit low-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopic technology, along with reverse genetics approaches to study hemozoin, a natural malaria parasite biomarker with unique magnetic properties and which biological pathway to its formation, is somehow related with most of the known antimalarial drugs. We have characterized the parasite at different morphological stages using low-field NMR in order to define the paramagnetic interactions and the exchange dynamics of parasite-resistant strains. From these measurements, we successfully characterized the entire intraerythrocytic cycle of the Plasmodium falciparum parasite linking some behavioral time-domain NMR patterns to specific physiological changes such as the specific time-point parasites move to a new stage development. To explore the capability of detecting distinct NMR features related with disturbance in haem detoxification pathway, we focused on the study of PfMDR2, a heavy metal transporter and on plasmepsins, aspartic proteases that degrade haemoglobin inside the parasite food vacuole. We designed a strategy to KO pfmdr2 into P. falciparum Dd2 strain and performed a haem fractionation assay on previously genetic engineered parasites over-expressing plasmepsins. The low-field NMR fingerprints obtained from this study was capable to distinguish parasite stage and parasitaemia as low as 0.01% and revealed high potential to further exploit the magnetic balance between haem species and its possible correlation with parasite susceptibility to drugs. Future studies are needed to explore better the role of this transporter and enzymes in the balance of the haem species and their ability to deliver distinct phenotypic NMR fingerprints. Given the portability characteristics of a low-field NMR device, the capture of specific NMR fingerprint could provide a proof-of-concept towards potential delivery of future precision malaria medicine, at the patients side.

title: Closed-loop system for real-time compulsive behavior detection and optogenetic stimulation in obsessive-compulsive disorder
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a prevalent neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by recurrent intrusive thoughts (obsessions) that can lead to repetitive behaviors (compulsions), which can cause significant disruption of daily activities. To simultaneously study the neuronal circuits involved in OCD and test novel therapies in a pre-clinical setting, it is critical to develop methodologies that can automatically detect and/or predict compulsive behavior and allow effective modulation of relevant brain circuits with temporal precision. Thus, we developed a closed-loop system that combines computer vision and machine learning approaches for effective real-time detection of compulsive/repetitive behaviors in the Sapap3 KO mouse model of OCD, with a wirelessly controlled optogenetic brain stimulator. Accurate online detection of repetitive behavioral motifs, such as face grooming, was achieved by combining DeepLabCut for real-time animal body part tracking with supervised extraction of kinematic behavioral features and classification of behavioral states with Decisions trees and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The highest classification sensitivity and specificity were achieved with decision trees, with 85.1% and 98.3%, respectively. A battery-powered optical brain stimulator in a lightweight PCB (1.43 g) with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication was also developed and programmed. Online detection of repetitive behavior triggers the BLE transmitter to send a writing request, with a latency inferior to 6.67 ms. The complete closed-loop system achieves a minimum latency of only 29.9 ms between the moment a BLE signal is sent, and the optical brain stimulator responds with user defined stimulation parameters. This new closed-loop system allows a direct assessment of the impact of brain circuit manipulations in compulsive behavior, contributing to the elucidation of the brain circuits involved in OCD and novel therapies developments.

title: Unravelling the role of the spinocerebellar ataxia type 3-associated protein ATXN3 in glioblastoma
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and malignant type of glioma in adults. Despite the efforts to investigate various treatments, GBM patients exhibit a rapid and unfavorable clinical evolution, with a median overall survival of only 15 months after diagnosis. Furthermore, the high proliferative activity, and heterogeneous and complex nature of GBM is associated with an unpredictable and distinct clinical outcome. Thus, the identification of molecular prognostic markers that allow the categorization of subgroups of patients with GBM is critical to contribute to the improvement of their clinical outcome. Ataxin-3 (ATXN3), the protein involved in the neurodegenerative disease Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3 (SCA3), is an evolutionarily conserved and ubiquitously expressed protein, which has been proposed to act as a deubiquitinating enzyme. In addition to its involvement in SCA3, ATXN3 was suggested to play a role in cancer, performing oncogenic or tumor suppressive functions depending on the tumor type. Since no study to date has explored the potential involvement of ATXN3 in gliomas, and particularly in GBM, in this work we intend, for the first time, to evaluate the functional role of ATXN3 in GBM and the clinical relevance of this protein in this deadly disease. We observed that ATXN3 expression decreases significantly with glioma grade, being less expressed in GBM when compared to lower-grade gliomas, and that it is associated with IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion. Specifically in GBM cells, we observed that ATXN3 is expressed in all cell models tested, both at the mRNA and protein level. Functionally, ATXN3 overexpression was associated with a significant decrease in the cell viability and invasion of GBM in vitro models, although no statistically significant effect was observed regarding cell proliferation and migration. This data suggests that ATXN3 may have tumor suppressive functions in GBM, decreasing its aggressiveness in vitro. In GBM patients, we found that ATXN3 has clinical prognostic value, being associated with longer overall survival, independently of other potential prognostic factors. In summary, this work allowed the understanding of the role of ATXN3 in GBM by identifying it as a tumor suppressor gene, and as a new prognostic biomarker of favorable outcome, bringing new knowledge about the molecular mechanisms underlying this deadly disease.

title: Graphene field-effect transistors functionalization for neurotransmitter biosensing
abstract: The understanding of how the brain works is fundamental for the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic methodologies for brain disorders. Graphene, due to its unique properties, is being increasingly used in a wide range of novel biomedical applications and is an emerging material for biosensing, including in the brain. Dopamine is a critical neurotransmitter, the chemical messages produced by brain cells, is dopamine, which is involved in various functions from motor control to learning. Thus, dopamine dysfunction underlies several brain disorders, including Parkinson’s Disease, schizophrenia and substance abuse. Striving to obtain a more sensitive and selective method of detection for dopamine, we engineered a new bioelectronic sensor for dopamine detection in this work. Electrolyte-gated graphene field-effect transistors’ monolayer graphene channel was functionalized with a molecular linker and a probe, a dopamine-specific DNA aptamer. When this receptor binds with dopamine, the redistribution of electronic charges on the graphene surface generates a change in the electric field which alters the electronic conductivity in the channel and overall device response. By tracking the changes in conductivity with the addition of known concentrations of dopamine calibration curves for our sensors were established. To do so, dopamine detection experiments were carried out in vitro in phosphate buffered saline solution and artificial cerebrospinal fluid electrolytic solutions. In PBS the obtained limit of detection (LOD) was of 1 aM, the lowest ever reported for a dopamine sensor, while in aCSF the LOD was of 10 aM. The sensors selectivity was also tested by comparing responses to dopamine with responses to dopamine precursors such as L-DOPA and L-tyrosine, and biological interferents as ascorbic acid. The use of a dopamine specific-aptamer allowed an outstanding selectivity, with the sensors producing negligeable responses to the other tested molecules. The excellent selectivity and sensitivity of our sensors allowed us the performance of ex vivo experiments with samples extracted from mice. Our novel sensors were used to show that reserpine, a drug that can deplete dopamine from brain synapses, was effective in reducing dopamine content in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) extracted from reserpine injected mice by 5-fold compared with controls. Taking advantage of brain homogenate samples that were depleted of dopamine by the action of reserpine, the ability of our sensors to perform detection in such a complex media was confirmed by adding known concentrations of dopamine to these samples. Although an expected loss of sensitivity was observed, the LOD in these complex samples was of 0.1 fM. These ground-breaking results allow us to consider further experiments in an in vivo setting.

title: Assessing the role of Sorting Nexins in the nervous system: insights from “stressed” synapses
abstract: Sorting Nexins (SNXs) have emerged as a family of highly conserved proteins that facilitate protein trafficking and intracellular signaling being key regulators of endocytic processes underlying synaptic plasticity and cognition. Interestingly, SNXs mis-regulation has been associated with neurological disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Down’s syndrome (DS). Particularly, SNX27 was shown to be a major contributor to intellectual impairments in DS. A study developed in a DS mouse model demonstrated that downregulation of SNX27 contributes to synaptic dysfunction and cognitive deficits by decreasing the recycling of glutamate receptors to the cell surface. Other SNXs, such as SNX3 and SNX12, have also been shown to be relevant for nervous system homeostasis regulation being associated with neurodevelopment and neurodegeneration. Despite this, much is unknown concerning SNXs’ expression and function within the nervous system, and particularly how they are modulated by stress, a condition linked to endocytic dysregulation, and a known inducer of cognitive decline and synaptic malfunction. Using both rodents and an established cell line, we set out to unveil SNXs role on the central nervous system and to study the modulatory effects of stress on behavioral performance, neuronal morphology and subcellular localization of regulators of synaptic plasticity. For such, we generated a SNX27+/- mouse model backcrossed to C57BL/6J background and characterized the impact of SNX27 reduction on postnatal development and behavioral performance, particularly under chronic stress-exposure. Furthermore, we explored the pharmacological modulation of phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate (PI3P) and glucocorticoids (GC) on SNXs expression in an established neuronal-like cell line. Our results indicate that reduced levels of SNX27 do not interfere with the acquisition of somatic and neurological development milestones. Concomitantly, behavioral analysis showed that the well-being of SNX27+/- C57BL/6J animals is affected and that these animals display increased anxious-like behaviors in the NSF test. Interestingly, we did not find any cognitive deficits in SNX27+/- C57BL/6J mice. In vitro findings indicate that SNX27 levels are increased under conditions of PI3P reduction or elevation of GC levels, which is not observed for SNX3. This might be indicative of opposing roles of SNX3 and SNX27 upon endolysosomal trafficking modulation. Overall, this work provides new insights on SNX27 role during development and behavioral performance in a pure genetic background, and how SNX27 is affected by stress-related processes as well as on the subcellular localization and modulation of additional SNXs by the above-mentioned.

title: Valence in the Nucleus Accumbens - identifying neural populations in appetitive and aversive responses
abstract: The nucleus accumbens (NAc) is recognized as an essential component of the reward circuit, being associated with processing of both rewarding and aversive events, and contributing for motivated behaviours. The NAc is a “limbic-motor interface”, and evidence shows its involvement in valence encoding – the intrinsic value of a given experience and consequent emotional and motivational responses. The NAc is mainly constituted by GABAergic medium spiny neurons (MSNs), divided into those expressing dopamine receptor D1 (D1-MSNs) and those expressing dopamine receptor D2 (D2-MSNs). These populations have been traditionally segregated anatomically (direct vs indirect pathway) and functionally (reward and positive valence vs aversion and negative valence). However, many recent studies have challenged this simplistic segregation. Yet, it is still uncertain which neuronal populations encode valence in the NAc, and this is a crucial question in the understanding of disorders with emotional deficits. In this thesis work we evaluated the neuronal activation levels associated with negative- (footshock) or positive-valence stimuli (cocaine) in the NAc, using the basolateral (BLA) and central (CeA) amygdala as control regions, used because they encode valence. We also characterized a c-fos-driven viral vector in order to establish a neuronal activation labelling strategy for future work. Furthermore, we performed optogenetic activation of stimulus-responsive neurons in the BLA, using the same vector, to induce valence-specific behavioural responses and validate our methodology. Our data shows that the NAc core (NAcc) and the BLA contain neuronal populations that respond to shock, measured by a higher c-fos+ cell density in comparison to controls. However, cocaine induced no significant changes in neuronal activation. Regarding the vector (driving channelrhodopsin-eYFP expression), we found that 16h-post stimulus exposure would be the more adequate timeframe to observe neuronal labelling. When using this vector and exposing mice to positive or negative stimuli, densitometry fluorescence data showed only a tendency for higher neuronal activation in the BLA after footshock, with no effects in the NAc, in comparison with control animals; with no effects due to cocaine. Lastly, optogenetic activation of footshock-responsive neurons in the BLA induced a tendency for avoidance in a real time place preference test (RTPP), yet this same activation did not induce conditioned place preference (CPP). While our data show neuronal activation in the NAcc and BLA in response to shock, the lack of differences with cocaine exposure together with densitometry and optogenetics data, indicates the need to develop new tools to label valence encoding neurons in the NAc.

title: Deciphering the mechanisms underlying the role of interleukin-10 in cognitive function
abstract: Cognitive function refers to internal mental processes critical for daily life activities, such as memory. Brain immune surveillance has proven to be crucial for cognitive function. T cell absence and increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines have been associated with impaired cognition. However, the role of anti-inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-10 (IL-10), has been poorly studied. Here, the effect of IL-10 absence in cognitive function was investigated in young-adult female BALB/c IL-10 knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) littermate mice. IL-10 absence impaired the hippocampal-dependent spatial reference memory in the Barnes-maze test. Interestingly, in this test, IL-10 KO mice showed a reduction in hippocampal-dependent strategies mainly during the metestrus and diestrus phases of the estrous cycle. No locomotor disabilities were observed in IL-10 KO mice however IL-10 deficiency impaired exploration in the open-field test. Although IL-10 absence has led to higher basal levels of corticosterone and increased gene expression levels of pro-inflammatory markers in the colon, these parameters did not correlate with the behavioral performance. Using the behavioral variables analyzed, the genotype (WT vsIL-10 KO) was classified by support vector machine models with an accuracy of up to 89.3%. Moreover, IL-10 absence led to a decreased number of neurons and volumetric atrophy of the dorsal, but not of the ventral hippocampus. Additionally, in the hippocampus, IL-10 deficiency negatively modulated the dendritic spine dynamics and decreased the dendritic arborization of dorsal and ventral dentate gyrus granule neurons and cornu ammonis-1 and -3 pyramidal neurons, which are known to support learning and memory. Furthermore, flow cytometry analysis showed that IL-10 absence impacted the leukocyte profile in the blood by increasing the total number of neutrophils and its percentage within leukocytes and decreasing the percentage of eosinophils, natural-killer cells, B cells, and T cells within leukocytes. Also, in the blood, IL-10 deficiency increased the percentage of effector memory CD4+ T cells, which were previously associated with a worst cognitive function of healthy aged individuals. IL-10 absence also increased the total number of leukocytes in the deep cervical lymph nodes, suggesting an increased cell recruitment to the lymphatic system of the brain. Lastly, through an antibiotic treatment, a protocol for gut microbiome depletion of IL-10 KO mice was optimized. After 3 days of treatment, antibiotics reduced the gene expression levels of 16s in the feces without fungal overgrowth, providing an initial step to explore the role of the gut microbiome in the cognitive function of IL-10 KO mice. Overall, these results not only supported that IL-10 absence impacted cognitive abilities but also highlighted the potential mechanisms underlying the action of this anti-inflammatory cytokine, which may be important contributors to the development of new IL-10-based therapies for cognitive impairments.

title: Combining stem cells secretome and N-acetylcysteine to Parkinson's Disease modeling and repair
abstract: Parkinson ‘s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a massive loss of dopaminergic neurons (DAn), leading to the appearance of several motor impairments. Current treatment is focused on mitigating the symptoms through the administration of levodopa, rather than on preventing DA neuronal damage. Therefore, the use and development of neuroprotective/disease-modifying strategies is an absolute need that can lead to promising gains on PD translational research. For instance, N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a natural compound with strong antioxidant effects, has been shown to modulate oxidative stress, preventing dopamine-induced cell death. Despite the evidence of neuroprotective and modulatory effects of this drug, as far as we know, it does not induce per se any regenerative process. Therefore, it would be of interest to combine NAC potentialities with innovative therapies that induce DAn repair, as mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) secretome, which has already revealed promising effects in the modulation of DA cell viability/preservation. Bearing this in mind, the main goal of the present thesis was to explore the therapeutic potential of MSCs secretome-mediated regenerative effects combined with the disease-modifying effects of NAC on the motor and histological deficits of a striatal 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) rat model of PD. From the results, we have successfully established the striatal model of PD, producing a retrograde degeneration of the DAn. After treatment intervention, we have observed that MSCs secretome and NAC (as monotherapy) were able to improve animals motor coordination and DAn histological deficits. Surprisingly, when combined with each other, although positive effects were observed to the motor and histological PD deficits, the obtained results did not surpass the effects of the single used strategies, which can be an indication that NAC and MSCs secretome may impact similar targets/mechanisms creating antagonistic effects. Nevertheless, based on the present results, understanding the complexity of NAC and secretome potentialities, and how its therapeutical properties interact with the cellular and molecular PD mechanisms may lead to a rational design of new therapeutic strategies for its functional modeling and repair.

title: Macrophages in pulmonary fibrosis: characterization and fibroblasts transdifferentiation modulation
abstract: A Fibrose pulmonar idiopática (FPI) é a forma mais comum e letal das doenças intersticiais pulmonares, afetando cerca de 3 milhões de pessoa no mundo. FPI é caracterizada pela perda progressiva/irreversível da capacidade respiratória como consequência da destruição da estrutura pulmonar. Sabe-se que a doença envolve ciclos de dano epitelial, acumulação exacerbada de miofibroblastos e consequente deposição excessiva de matriz extracelular. Mais recentemente o foco da investigação destas doenças tem sido a compreensão do papel da inflamação na sua progressão, como por exemplo das populações de macrófagos pulmonares (MO). As funções dos macrófagos alveolares (AMs) e intersticiais (IMs) que se encontram descritas na literatura são controversas. Assim, o objetivo principal desta tese foi contribuir com novos conhecimentos sobre se os AMs e IMs modulam diferencialmente a progressão da fibrose, nomeadamente através da interação com fibroblastos, durante a fase inflamatória, utilizando para tal o modelo de ratinho de fibrose pulmonar induzido por bleomicina (BLM). Primeiramente, a caracterização de MO foi realizada por citometria de fluxo (CF), no pulmão de ratinhos normais não tratados, tratados com o veículo da BLM e tratados com BLM, aos dias 3, 5, 7 e 9 após a sua administração. Os pulmões de ratinho tratados apresentaram um aumento significativo e progressivo na quantidade de IMs. Além disto, a expressão de CD80, CD206 e MHCII também foi verificada por CF, em que foi observado um aumento da expressão dos marcadores mencionados nos IMs tratados. No dia 7 após administração de BLM, os MO de células pulmonares de ratinhos tratados com BLM e não tratados foram obtidos por separação celular com recurso a CF para posterior análise de níveis de expressão de transcritos de genes associados à resposta pró-inflamatória e anti-inflamatória, por qRT-PCR. Observou-se o aumento da expressão de vários genes pelos IMs tratados, cuja ação está na sua generalidade associada à promoção de um microambiente pró-fibrótico. Em segundo lugar, e de forma a responder se os AMs e IMs modulam diferencialmente a progressão da fibrose por interação com fibroblastos, uma linha celular de fibroblastos de pulmão de ratinho foi estimulada com meio condicionado de MO, obtidos por separação celular com recurso a citometria de fluxo, nos dias 7 e 9 após a administração de BLM. Posteriormente, foi feita a análise de apoptose, proliferação, atividade metabólica e estado de transdiferenciação dos fibroblastos. Em geral, verificamos que nos ensaios in vitro de 7 dias, os meios condicionados derivados de IMs de animais tratados apresentavam maior capacidade de transdiferenciação de fibroblastos. Em conjunto, os dados desta tese indicam que, no pico da fase inflamatória (dia 7), a população de IMs é a população crucial na promoção da progressão da fibrose.

title: Sporothrix brasiliensis genetic toolbox
abstract: A esporotricose é a micose subcutânea mais prevalente e distribuída no mundo. A espécie S. brasiliensis é descrita como sendo a mais virulenta, estando associada com manifestações clínicas mais severas, contudo, os mecanismos subjacentes à infeção e virulência de Sporothrix spp. ainda carecem de clarificação. Durante os últimos anos, o genoma de várias espécies de Sporothrix foi totalmente sequenciado e os dados estão disponíveis em recursos de acesso aberto. Em contraste, esse conhecimento genómico não foi acompanhado pelo desenvolvimento de ferramentas de genética reversa, que poderiam contribuir para a decodificação das funções dos genes. O presente trabalho focou-se na criação de uma caixa de ferramentas genéticas, permitindo a criação de uma biblioteca de transformantes que podem ser usados no futuro em estudos com o objetivo de desvendar os mecanismos pouco conhecidos de virulência do S. brasiliensis. Para tal, testamos um sistema CRIPR/Cas9 para S. brasiliensis. Contudo, os nossos resultados sugerem que o promotor TEF1-α, presente no plasmídeo utilizado, pPTS608, desenhado para Aspergillus spp., não é capaz de expressar a maquinaria CRISPR/Cas9 no sistema biológico de S. brasiliensis. Neste sentido, o nosso trabalho focou-se na avaliação do potencial de diferentes promotores e no desenvolvimento de um conjunto de transformantes de S. brasiliensis. Os nossos resultados mostram que a expressão induzida pelo promotor GAPDH resultou numa alta e constitutiva expressão genética de proteínas de fluorescência em transformantes de S. brasiliensis. Assim, desenvolvemos um conjunto de plasmídeos para clonagem com o promotor GAPDH ou H2A para a expressão de proteínas fluorescentes (GFP e mCherry). Estes plasmídeos permitem a clonagem de qualquer gene para expressão em fusão N-terminal in-frame com proteínas fluorescentes vermelhas ou verdes. Os transformantes de S. brasiliensis apresentam fluorescência localizada no núcleo quando a fusão in-frame foi feita com a histona endógena H2A, demonstrando a utilidade desses plasmídeos para clonagem de genes e proteínas fluorescentes em fusão. Em soma, os nossos resultados confirmam o sucesso na elaboração de protocolos para a construção de plasmídeos fáceis de editar e na criação de um conjunto de transformantes de S. brasiliensis através da Transformação Mediada por Agrobacterium tumefaciens (ATMT). A criação desta caixa de ferramentas genéticas, irá permitir no futuro elucidar os mecanismos de virulência pouco conhecidos do S. brasiliensis.

title: Fluorescent tag Sporothrix brasiliensis: a tool for host-pathogen interaction studies
abstract: A esporotricose é um problema de saúde emergente e a micose subcutânea mais prevalente no mundo. Esta doença ocorre em hospedeiros mamíferos, o que facilita a sua transmissão zoonótica. A transformação mediada por Agrobacterium tumefaciens (ATMT) é uma técnica amplamente utilizada para a transformação de plantas e fungos. No presente trabalho, estabelecemos um sistema de ATMT para S. brasiliensis, considerando diferentes estirpes de A. tumefaciens e S. brasiliensis, bem como várias condições de co-cultivo. Os nossos resultados apontam para 72h de co-cultivo a 26°C, a estirpe bacteriana AGL-1 e o rácio de 2:1 (bactérias:fungos) como condições ideais para a obtenção de um elevado número de transformantes. Nestas condições, obtivemos 3179 ± 1171 transformantes/co cultivo. A análise de RT-PCR demostrou a presença de uma cópia do gene HPH. A análise de FACS mostrou alta estabilidade mitótica do gene GFP dos isolados da estirpe pGAPDH::GFP. Os mutantes pGAPDH::GFP e pGAPDH::H2A::GFP de S. brasiliensis foram respetivamente usados para calcular o índice de fagocitose e a atividade fungicida. A expressão citoplasmática de GFP da estirpe de pGAPDH::GFP permitiu uma forte visualização de fluorescência dentro dos monócitos/macrófagos em análises de microscópica e FACS. Relativamente aos mutantes pGAPDH::H2A::GFP S. brasiliensis não foi possível obter uma correlação entre a perda de viabilidade fúngica ou morte fúngica e a perda de fluorescência GFP em todos as experiências realizadas no que diz respeito à avaliação da capacidade fungicida dos monócitos/macrófagos. Para além disso, não foi possível detetar a sua fluorescência GFP após ter sido fagocitado pelos monócitos/macrófagos em análises de microscópica e FACS. Em primeiro lugar, este trabalho permitiu a criação de uma ferramenta genética eficiente para construir bibliotecas de transformantes em larga escala para S. brasiliensis. Em segundo lugar, os nossos resultados demostraram que o mutante pGAPDH::GFP pode ser usado em ensaios de fagocitose sem a necessidade de coloração com fluoróforo antes da infeção. Em soma, os nossos resultados podem ajudar a entender melhor as interações hospedeiro-patógeno e o mecanismo de virulência da Sporothrix spp..
